trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or the RENFE train (€4.60) to the city center. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Drop off luggage, freshen up, and take a short relaxing stroll along Barceloneta Beach promenade — it's lively even late at night in August. Grab a late-night snack nearby.

meals.dinner: Late-night bite at a 24-hour kebab shop or a local bar near Barceloneta — budget €5–8. Try a bocadillo (Spanish sandwich) from a nearby kiosk.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival — it will save money throughout the trip. Keep arrival night simple and low-key to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a walk along Barceloneta Beach to enjoy the morning sea breeze. Head to the nearby Mercat de Santa Caterina (a lesser-known but stunning alternative to La Boqueria) for a free architectural marvel and cheap fresh fruit breakfast. Then walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for a self-guided walking tour — explore narrow medieval streets, Plaça Reial, and the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Picasso Museum exterior and the El Born neighborhood — stroll through its charming streets and visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, stunning Gothic architecture). Walk along Passeig del Born and browse local boutiques. Head to Parc de la Ciutadella (free) for a relaxing afternoon — rent a rowboat on the lake for €6/person or simply enjoy the fountain and green space.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Barceloneta area for dinner. After dinner, explore the beach nightlife scene — beach bars (chiringuitos) along Barceloneta come alive in August. Enjoy a cheap beer or sangria while listening to live music. The area around Rambla del Poblenou is great for a budget-friendly evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastry from Mercat de Santa Caterina — budget €3–5
meals.lunch: Menú del día (fixed lunch menu) at a local restaurant in the Gothic Quarter — 3 courses including drink for €10–13. Look for spots away from Las Ramblas for better value.
meals.dinner: Chiringuito beach bar near Barceloneta — grilled fish or paella for €8–12. Or try a local pizzeria or falafel spot for €6–8.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak summer in Barcelona — mornings are the best time to visit popular sites before crowds and heat peak. Wear sunscreen and carry a water bottle. The Gothic Quarter is very walkable from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to the iconic Sagrada Família — book tickets online in advance to save time (€26 basic entry, worth every cent for architecture lovers). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, both interior and exterior. Afterward, walk through the Eixample neighborhood to admire the grid-style modernist city planning and spot other Gaudí and Domènech i Montaner buildings from the outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) exterior for free photo opportunities — interior tickets are expensive (€25+), so admire the extraordinary facades from the street on Passeig de Gràcia. Then head to Gràcia neighborhood — a bohemian, local district with charming plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Browse vintage shops and street art. Visit Park Güell — the monumental zone requires a ticket (€10), but the surrounding free park areas offer great views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the city center. Explore the El Raval neighborhood for pre-dinner drinks at a budget bar. Try vermouth (vermut) culture — a quintessential Barcelona tradition — at a local bar for €2–3 a glass. After dinner, check out the nightlife on Carrer de Blai (famous for pintxos bars) for cheap evening snacks and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant at a local café near the hotel — budget €3–4
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Sagrada Família or Eixample — €11–13 for a full 3-course meal
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai in El Raval — pintxos from €1–2 each, budget €8–12 total for a satisfying meal with drinks

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least a week in advance online to guarantee entry and avoid long queues. Park Güell free zones are accessible anytime but get crowded by midday — try visiting in the late afternoon for better light and fewer tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus up to Montjuïc — use the T-Casual card for the metro, then walk or take the free funicular (included with metro card) up the hill. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for panoramic views of Barcelona and the sea. Explore the castle grounds and enjoy the scenery. Walk down through the Jardins de Laribal (free) — beautiful terraced gardens on the hillside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (Barcelona Pavilion) — a masterpiece of modernist architecture and very affordable at €5 entry. Then explore the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc — a hip, local area with street art, independent cafés, and a relaxed vibe. Walk along Avinguda del Paral·lel and check out the MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya) exterior and its famous cascading fountains — free to admire from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest and freshen up for a proper Barcelona night out. Head to El Born or Barceloneta around 22:00 (Barcelona nightlife starts late). Visit a rooftop bar for sunset drinks — several offer free entry with a drink purchase. Later, explore the club scene around Port Olímpic (walking distance from the hotel) — many clubs have free entry before midnight with a flyer or guest list.

meals.breakfast: Toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet) and orange juice at a local café in Barceloneta — budget €4–6. A true Catalan staple.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc — grab supplies from a nearby Mercadona or Lidl supermarket (baguette, cheese, cured meats, fruit) for €5–7 total
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant in Poble Sec — try a traditional Catalan restaurant with menú del día (some serve it at dinner too) for €12–15, or grab tapas at a bar for €8–10

day_by_day.notes: The Montjuïc Magic Fountain show (Font Màgica) runs on selected evenings in summer — check the schedule online as it's completely free and spectacular. Port Olímpic clubs can have cover charges after midnight (€10–15) — arrive early or get on a guest list via apps like Xceed or Fever for free or discounted entry.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final morning swim at Barceloneta Beach — one of the great perks of the beachfront hotel location. Pack up and check out. Take a final stroll along La Barceloneta promenade and stop at a local café for a farewell breakfast. If time allows, pop into La Boqueria market on Las Ramblas for a quick browse and a fresh juice (€2–3) — best experienced early morning before tourist crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, spend remaining hours in the Gothic Quarter for any last-minute souvenir shopping — avoid tourist trap shops on Las Ramblas and instead browse the small independent shops on Carrer del Pi or Carrer de la Palla for affordable gifts. Head to the airport via Aerobus (€5.90) or RENFE train (€4.60) — allow at least 2.5 hours before departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Spanish breakfast at a local café — café con leche, fresh OJ, and toast with tomato and olive oil — budget €4–6
meals.lunch: Quick and budget-friendly lunch near the Gothic Quarter or airport — bocadillo sandwich from a café (€4–6) or a meal at the airport if time is tight (budget €10–15 at airport prices)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time in advance — standard is 12:00 noon. Many hotels offer luggage storage for a few hours if your flight is in the late afternoon or evening. Keep your T-Casual metro card — any remaining trips are valid. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): €40–60/day covering transport, meals, and key attraction entries.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Focus on reaching Aegean Bliss Resort in Beachfront area. Allow time for baggage claim, customs, and a 30–40 min taxi or Aerobus transfer to the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — still in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and take a short 10-minute walk along the Barceloneta beachfront promenade to decompress. Grab a late-night bite at a nearby 24-hour tapas bar or hotel bar before resting.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: On the plane or at Barcelona El Prat Airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby chiringuito or hotel bar near Barceloneta — try pan con tomate and jamón ibérico (€10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — only the beachfront stroll is suggested post-arrival. Set alarms for an early start on Day 2. Pre-book a taxi or check Aerobus schedules in advance to avoid delays after landing.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Start the day with a skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Book the 9:00 AM slot to beat the crowds. Marvel at the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior columns, and climb a tower for panoramic city views. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Head north by metro (L3 to Lesseps or Vallcarca) to Gaudí's whimsical Park Güell. Explore the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the hypostyle room. Spend the remaining afternoon wandering the bohemian Gràcia neighborhood — browse independent boutiques, colorful plazas like Plaça del Sol, and local cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Gràcia followed by a relaxed evening stroll back toward the hotel. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try a croissant with café amb llet (coffee with milk) at a local bakery (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in the Gràcia neighborhood — try Cervecería Catalana or a local menú del día (set lunch menu with starter, main, drink, and dessert for €12–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Gràcia restaurant — try La Pepita or similar for creative Catalan tapas (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Park Güell's Monumental Zone also requires timed-entry tickets (€10); book online. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Dive into Barcelona's medieval heart with a guided walking tour of the Gothic Quarter. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the stunning Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and narrow labyrinthine streets. Tours typically run 9:30–11:30 AM. Ideal for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas Crawl on El Born — Transition seamlessly from the Gothic Quarter into the adjacent El Born neighborhood for a self-guided or small-group tapas crawl. Visit standout spots like Bar del Pla, El Xampanyet, and Paradiso cocktail bar. Explore the stunning El Born Cultural Centre (former iron market) and the Picasso Museum exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife Experience in Barceloneta & Port Olímpic — Begin with sunset cocktails at a beachfront chiringuito in Barceloneta around 8:00 PM. Dine at a seafood restaurant on the beach, then head to Port Olímpic for Barcelona's legendary club and bar scene. Clubs typically get lively after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a Gothic Quarter café before the tour — try Caelum for traditional Catalan sweets (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Tapas crawl in El Born — budget €20–25 per person across multiple stops for patatas bravas, croquetas, anchovies, and cava
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner in Barceloneta — try La Cova Fumada (arrive early, cash only) or La Mar Salada for fresh paella or fideuà (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter tour is best done in the morning before heat peaks in August. El Born tapas crawl flows naturally afterward. For nightlife, pace yourself — Barcelona's clubs don't fill until 1:00–2:00 AM. Carry cash for smaller tapas bars.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Barceloneta — After a late night, enjoy a slow morning. Walk directly from the Aegean Bliss Resort to Barceloneta Beach. Swim, sunbathe, and recharge. Explore the beachfront promenade and grab breakfast at a nearby café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Passeig de Gràcia Architecture Walk — Take the metro or a leisurely stroll up to Passeig de Gràcia to explore Barcelona's most famous modernist boulevard. Visit the exterior and interior of Casa Batlló (book timed entry) and admire Casa Milà (La Pedrera) and Casa Amatller on the 'Block of Discord.' Browse the upscale Eixample neighborhood and its grid-patterned streets.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience in the Eixample — Enjoy sundowner drinks at a rooftop bar such as the one at Hotel Majestic or Azimut Rooftop for sweeping city views. Follow with dinner in the Eixample before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Beachside café breakfast — fresh orange juice, toast with tomato and olive oil, and a tortilla española (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near Passeig de Gràcia — try Cervecería Catalana (popular, may have a short wait) for montaditos and tapas (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner in Eixample — try Parking Pizza for a relaxed vibe or Bodega Sepúlveda for Catalan wine and charcuterie (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló tickets are pricey (€29–35) but worth it for architecture enthusiasts — the interior is extraordinary. La Pedrera rooftop is also spectacular at sunset if you prefer it over a bar. August heat peaks in the afternoon, so the beach morning is well-timed.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Poble Sec exploration — Take the cable car or metro to Montjuïc hill for sweeping views over Barcelona and the port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (mid-range entry, excellent modern art) or the Montjuïc Castle for architecture and history. Walk through the gardens for a peaceful start to the final day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting at Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria on La Rambla or the El Born boutiques. Pick up local products — olive oil, saffron, cava, and artisan goods. Take a final walk along La Rambla toward the sea and the Columbus Monument.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in El Born or Barceloneta — Return to your favorite neighborhood for a memorable last meal. Reflect on the trip over a bottle of Catalan wine and a spread of sharing plates.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final visit to a local café — try a full Catalan breakfast with pa amb tomàquet, cold cuts, and coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at La Boqueria market — fresh fruit, jamón, cheese, and a glass of cava standing at a market bar (€12–18)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a well-regarded El Born or Barceloneta restaurant — try El Xampanyet for classic Catalan atmosphere or Barraca for beachside seafood (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure flight time and plan accordingly — if flying the next day, this full Day 5 is yours. If departing on the 19th, adjust the afternoon and evening to allow sufficient airport transfer time (30–45 min to El Prat). Keep luggage stored at the hotel until departure if needed.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Barcelona El Prat Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity, and enjoy the resort's late-night room service.
day_by_day.evening: After settling in, head to the resort's rooftop bar or beachfront lounge for a nightcap. Enjoy a light late-night supper from the hotel's 24-hour in-room dining menu featuring Catalan charcuterie boards and cava to decompress after the flight.

meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — Catalan charcuterie board, pan con tomate, and a bottle of cava from the premium minibar selection

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the concierge. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon arrival. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue before a full schedule begins Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning start. Enjoy a full luxury breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Afterwards, take a refreshing walk along the Barceloneta beachfront promenade to acclimate to the city. At around 11:00, embark on the Sagrada Família Guided Tour — a skip-the-line private guided experience of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Marvel at the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring forest-like interior nave, and the breathtaking stained-glass light displays. Opt for tower access for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, take a short taxi or private car to the Eixample district for a leisurely lunch. Post-lunch, stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the 'Block of Discord' — Gaudí's Casa Batlló, Domènech i Montaner's Casa Lleó Morera, and Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller. Consider a premium Casa Batlló after-hours or magic nights ticket for an immersive architectural experience. Return to the resort by 18:00 for a rest and sunset swim.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the evening with cocktails at a beachfront chiringuito near Barceloneta as the sun sets over the Mediterranean. Transition into Barcelona's legendary nightlife scene around Port Olímpic — experience the Nightlife Experience in Barceloneta & Port Olímpic, starting at upscale beach clubs and moving into the premium clubs at the port. Dress code smart-casual to elegant.

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — freshly squeezed juices, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, and Catalan cheeses
meals.lunch: Moments (2 Michelin stars) or Disfrutar (3 Michelin stars) in Eixample — book well in advance for a tasting menu experience featuring avant-garde Catalan cuisine
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) on Passeig Marítim — Mediterranean fusion cuisine with sea views, transitioning seamlessly into the evening lounge and nightlife scene

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família skip-the-line private guided tour at least 2–3 weeks in advance as tickets sell out quickly. Reserve Michelin-starred lunch months ahead. Carry the resort's concierge card for VIP nightclub entry arrangements.

day_by_day.morning: After a late night, enjoy a relaxed brunch at the resort. By 10:30–11:00, join the Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — a private guided walk through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the old Jewish quarter (El Call), and hidden plazas. A knowledgeable private guide will bring centuries of history to life with curated architectural and cultural commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: From the Gothic Quarter, walk across the Born bridge into the El Born neighborhood for an immersive afternoon. Explore the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture. Browse the high-end concept stores and galleries along Carrer del Rec and Passeig del Born. At around 16:00, begin the Tapas Crawl on El Born — a premium small-group or private guided tapas experience sampling patatas bravas, jamón ibérico de bellota, fresh seafood, and local vermouth at the neighborhood's finest bars and taverns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset swim and to freshen up. Enjoy a sophisticated dinner at one of Barcelona's top waterfront restaurants near the resort. Cap the evening with drinks at a rooftop cocktail bar in the Barceloneta area — consider Eclipse Bar at Hotel W Barcelona for its stunning 360-degree city and sea views.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at the resort's terrace restaurant — avocado toast, eggs any style, fresh fruit platters, and Catalan pastries with specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Integrated into the El Born Tapas Crawl — premium pintxos, ibérico ham, fresh anchovies, croquetas, and local craft beers or vermouths at curated El Born establishments
meals.dinner: Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona (1 Michelin star) — refined Mediterranean seafood tasting menu with an exceptional wine list, steps from the beachfront

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter tour as streets are cobblestoned. The tapas crawl typically runs 3–4 hours — pace yourself. Book Eclipse Bar or rooftop venue in advance for guaranteed seating with views.

day_by_day.morning: Start the morning with an early breakfast and depart by 09:30 for Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration. Arrive early to beat the crowds at Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park. A private guide will lead you through the mosaic Dragon Staircase, the Hypostyle Room, the iconic serpentine mosaic terrace with its sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona, and the gingerbread gatehouses. Visit the Casa Museu Gaudí within the park for an intimate look at the architect's personal life and design philosophy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Park Güell into the charming Gràcia neighborhood — one of Barcelona's most bohemian and architecturally rich districts. Explore the local plazas (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia), independent boutiques, and street art. After lunch, visit Casa Vicens — Gaudí's very first major work and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lesser-known but architecturally extraordinary. Return to the resort by 17:30 for a spa session at the resort's luxury wellness facilities before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: This evening is dedicated to Barcelona's world-class nightlife. Begin with a pre-dinner cocktail at the resort's beach bar at golden hour. Dinner at a celebrated restaurant in the Eixample or Barceloneta area. Post-dinner, experience Barcelona's iconic club scene — Pacha Barcelona, Opium Mar, or Shôko offer premium bottle service and world-class DJs. Arrange VIP table reservations through the hotel concierge for the best experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort — continental spread with fresh juices, Catalan pastries, and espresso to fuel the morning excursion
meals.lunch: La Pepita Gràcia or La Pepita Comerç — a beloved local gem in the Gràcia neighborhood offering creative Catalan tapas and natural wines in a beautifully designed space
meals.dinner: Bodega 1900 by Albert Adrià in Eixample — a refined reinvention of a classic Barcelona vermouth bar and tavern, celebrating traditional Catalan flavors with modern culinary mastery

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell monumental zone requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance. The park is busiest 10:00–14:00; arriving at 09:30 ensures a more peaceful experience. Arrange VIP nightclub table service at least 24 hours ahead through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: A leisurely final morning. Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the resort's oceanfront terrace. Take a final walk along the Barceloneta beach or a morning swim in the Mediterranean. If time permits, visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina or Mercat de la Boqueria for a sensory farewell to Barcelona's vibrant food culture — pick up artisan gifts, local olive oils, and premium Catalan products to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final light lunch near the resort or in the Gothic Quarter. Use remaining afternoon hours for last-minute shopping along Passeig de Gràcia — flagship stores of Spanish designers like Loewe, as well as international luxury houses. Check out from the resort and arrange a private luxury transfer back to Barcelona El Prat Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — farewell to Barcelona. If the flight is evening or overnight, consider a final sunset cocktail at the hotel bar before the transfer.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full spread including fresh-squeezed orange juice, smoked salmon, eggs royale, artisan cheeses, seasonal fruit, and champagne toast
meals.lunch: Bar Cañete in the Raval or Els Pescadors in Poblenou — celebrated for exceptional fresh seafood and traditional Catalan rice dishes; a perfect final culinary memory of Barcelona
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner near the resort if departure allows — alternatively, pack a premium picnic from the Mercat de la Boqueria for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort (typically available until 14:00–16:00 for premium guests) to maximize the final day without rushing. Confirm private airport transfer the night before. Keep passports and travel documents easily accessible for departure.
